assumptions_and_unknowns: Key semantic type is not claimed beyond the unsigned 64-bit comparison and modulo the binary shows.
The libstdc++ prime rehash policy behind the PLT call is not pinned; the model takes it as a caller-supplied callable and pins only the call contract.
The outer +0x00..+0x38 range (a vector in PR #1798's reading) is not touched by this window and not claimed here.
The mutex at +0x18 in PR #1798's reading is not touched by this window; only +0x78 is locked here.
Indirect reachability beyond the two direct callers is not claimed.

callee_find_or_insert.bucket_recompute: bucket recomputed as key mod new count after any rehash
callee_find_or_insert.count_zero_note: a zero bucket count divides by zero in the binary; the model raises InconsistentTable for it
callee_find_or_insert.element_count: increased by 1 on both insert paths
callee_find_or_insert.exception_pad: 0x5160dae..0x5160dbf: on exception the fresh node is freed with operator delete (size 0x18), then _Unwind_Resume; canary fs:0x28 at rsp+0x08, failure calls __stack_chk_fail at 0x5160da9
callee_find_or_insert.insert_after_before_node: bucket entry set: new node's next is the before-node's next, before-node's next is the new node, entry unchanged
callee_find_or_insert.insert_head_path: bucket entry unset: new node becomes the head, the old head's bucket entry (when there is an old head) is repointed at the new node, then this bucket's entry is the sentinel
callee_find_or_insert.lookup: same bucket segment walk as the window; a match returns the node's value slot
callee_find_or_insert.miss_allocation: fresh 0x18-byte node, next 0, key copied from [rsi], value 0

need_rehash_call.returns: need flag in al, new count in rdx
need_rehash_call.saved_next_resize: table+0x28 copied to the stack slot before the call and passed as the rehash aux third argument

callee_find_or_insert.returns: address of the node's value slot (+0x10)

callee_rehash_aux.allocation: count * 8 bytes via operator new, zeroed with memset
callee_rehash_aux.catch_pad: 0x5160be0: __cxa_begin_catch, table+0x28 restored from [saved pointer], __cxa_rethrow; 0x5160bf9: __cxa_end_catch and _Unwind_Resume; the pad is reachable from the operator new call, where the saved pointer is still live in r12; LSDA mapping not claimed
callee_rehash_aux.epilogue: old array freed with operator delete[] over old count * 8 unless the old pointer is the +0x30 slot; bucket count and buckets pointer committed; element count and policy untouched
callee_rehash_aux.migration: old head read from table+0x10 then reset to null; nodes walked in existing order; bucket is node key mod new count
callee_rehash_aux.migration_empty_bucket: prepend to the head, entry is the sentinel; when the displaced head is non-null, the previous bucket's entry is repointed at this node, then the previous index follows (previous starts 0, updates on the empty path only)
callee_rehash_aux.migration_nonempty_bucket: insert after the before-node, touching neither the fixup nor the previous index
callee_rehash_aux.note: This instantiation hashes at node +0x08 (the key itself); PR #1751's rehash aux at 0x515a820 is a different instantiation with the cached hash at node +0x70. The two are not duplicates: different node type, different caller families.
callee_rehash_aux.overflow_arms: count >> 60 nonzero: count >> 61 zero throws bad_alloc, otherwise bad_array_new_length
callee_rehash_aux.single_bucket_arm: new count 1 reuses the table+0x30 slot (zeroed qword), no allocation, overflow checks skipped

callers_of_rehash_aux.method: full executable-segment e8/e9 scans plus whole-file qword scan
callers_of_rehash_aux.note: The aux is shared across hashtable instantiations; only the 0x5160c10 call is modeled here.

callers_of_window.method: full executable-segment e8/e9 scans plus whole-file qword scan
callers_of_window.note: Both callers walk an Rb_tree (Rb_tree_increment at the loop tail) and pass a tree node's +0x28 field as the key; census only, the enclosing routines are not modeled here.

node_layout.bucket_entry: node before the first node of the bucket, the sentinel address (table+0x10) when the first node is the table head, or nothing when never written
node_layout.key_comparison: 64-bit equality; bucket is key modulo bucket count (unsigned division); no separate hash call, so the hash is the key itself for this instantiation

outer_layout.note: Offsets +0x40..+0x78 match PR #1798's pending-key table; the window never touches outer +0x00..+0x38, so that range is not claimed here.

relation_to_prior_items.1751: different rehash instantiation (cached hash at node +0x70); this item's aux is the +0x08-key instantiation
relation_to_prior_items.1798: same outer pending-key table shape (+0x40 hashtable, +0x58 element count, +0x78 mutex); the sweep erases from it, this window increments/inserts into it
relation_to_prior_items.1808: different struct (vector of counted pairs, mutex +0x18); same counted-key idea, different container

window.summary: mutex-guarded counted-key increment-or-insert over the hashtable at outer+0x40

window_behavior.bucket_path: element count != 0 takes a bucket walk: bucket = key mod bucket count, segment walk comparing keys, stopping at the chain end or at the first node whose bucket differs
window_behavior.count_zero_path: element count == 0 takes a linear chain walk from before-begin next; in a consistent table the head is null and this falls straight to the insert path
window_behavior.found: matching node's value field (+0x10) increased by 1 with addq (wraps modulo 2^64), mutex unlocked, return
window_behavior.found_null_arm: the found arm re-loads the before-node's next and falls to the insert path on null; recorded as observed, it cannot fire from a consistent walk because the node was just dereferenced
window_behavior.lock: mutex at outer+0x78 locked first; nonzero result throws system_error at 0x5160eaa
window_behavior.miss: calls find-or-insert 0x5160c10 with (table at outer+0x40, address of the key stack slot) and stores 1 into the returned value slot
window_behavior.unlock: mutex unlocked on the normal epilogue (0x5160e23) and on the exception path via the cleanup stub 0x5160dc0 (unlock, _Unwind_Resume)
